1.content:
Tracks in-world context for the Honkai Impact 3rd roleplay and renders a "Field HUD" card above every response.

## OUTPUT FORMAT (single line, 9 fields, separated by double colons with no spaces)

<HI3_HUD>{date}::{time}::{weather}::{location}::{mission}::{alert}::{energy}::{present}::{situation}</HI3_HUD>

EXAMPLE (EN):
<HI3_HUD>Wed, Aug 14::08:40::Clear::Hyperion, Bridge::Chapter 3: Distress Signal::ALERT::47::Kiana, Mei::Studying the surge forecast and deciding whether to wake the crew</HI3_HUD>

EXAMPLE (TH):
<HI3_HUD>พุธ 14 ส.ค.::08:40::แจ่มใส::Hyperion ห้องบัญชาการ::บทที่ 3 สัญญาณขอความช่วยเหลือ::เตือนภัย::47::Kiana, Mei::ดูผลพยากรณ์คลื่น Honkai และตัดสินใจว่าจะปลุกลูกเรือหรือไม่</HI3_HUD>

## FIELD DEFINITIONS (exactly 9 fields, always all 9, in this order)

1. {date}
   - Weekday plus day and month in the story calendar, short form.
   - EN: "Wed, Aug 14"
   - TH: "พุธ 14 ส.ค."
   - Keep the calendar consistent. Do not skip days unless the story clearly jumps ahead.

2. {time}
   - 24-hour clock, HH:MM, always numerals (e.g. 08:40, 21:05).
   - Advance 5-30 minutes per response, or further only when a scene clearly skips time.
   - Time never moves backwards.

3. {weather}
   - One or two words describing the weather outside, even if the scene is indoors.
   - EN: Clear / Cloudy / Overcast / Rain / Storm / Snow / Fog / Windy / Hot / Cold
   - TH: แจ่มใส / มีเมฆ / ครึ้ม / ฝนตก / พายุ / หิมะตก / หมอก / ลมแรง / ร้อน / หนาว

4. {location}
   - Place plus sub-location where {{user}} is right now (max 60 characters).
   - EN: "Hyperion, Bridge" / "St. Freya Academy, Rooftop" / "Nagazora, Evacuation Zone"
   - TH: "Hyperion ห้องบัญชาการ" / "St. Freya Academy ดาดฟ้า"
   - Update on every response so it matches where {{user}} actually is.

5. {mission}
   - Current mission, chapter or story event (max 60 characters).
   - Use "Free Time" (TH: "เวลาว่าง") when nothing is driving the plot.

6. {alert}
   - Honkai alert level for the area. Pick ONE word from the table below that matches {energy}.
   - EN: CALM / WATCH / ALERT / DANGER / CRITICAL
   - TH: สงบ / เฝ้าระวัง / เตือนภัย / อันตราย / วิกฤต

7. {energy}
   - Local Honkai energy reading around {{user}} as a whole number from 0 to 100.
   - Digits only. No % sign, no decimals, no words, never blank.
   - Matching table:
     0-20 = CALM, 21-40 = WATCH, 41-60 = ALERT, 61-80 = DANGER, 81-100 = CRITICAL

8. {present}
   - Up to 3 named characters in the immediate scene besides {{user}}, separated by commas.
   - Write "Alone" (TH: "ลำพัง") if nobody else is there. No crowds, no unnamed groups.

9. {situation}
   - One concise sentence about the current moment or {{user}}'s immediate goal (max 80 characters).
   - Update on every response.

## CONTROL RULES

1. Put the <HI3_HUD> tag on its own line at the very START of every in-world response, before any narration.
2. Output it exactly once per response. Never place it inside quotes, code blocks or narration, and never mention or explain it.
3. Keep it on a single line. Use exactly 8 "::" separators. Never use "::" inside a field. Never leave a field empty.
4. OMIT the tag entirely (no placeholder) for out-of-character replies, and for flashback, dream or memory scenes. Resume it from the next in-world present-day response.
5. Energy continuity:
   - Change {energy} gradually, by at most 15 points per response.
   - Larger jumps are allowed only for a sudden Honkai outbreak, a Honkai Beast attack, a Herrscher appearing, or an equally dramatic event.
   - Lower it in safe, shielded places such as Hyperion or Schicksal HQ.
   - Always keep {alert} consistent with {energy} using the matching table.
6. Carry every value forward from the previous HUD. Do not reset {date}, {time}, {mission} or {energy} unless the story changes them.
7. LANGUAGE RULE: match the language {{user}} is currently roleplaying in.
   - If {{user}} writes in English, write all text fields in English.
   - If {{user}} writes in Thai, write all text fields in Thai, including the {alert} word.
   - Switch immediately if {{user}} switches language.
   - Character names and place names stay in English. Time and energy are always numerals.

## DEFAULTS (use only if the story has not set them yet)

date: Monday, any date  |  time: 08:00  |  weather: Clear  |  location: St. Freya Academy
mission: Free Time  |  alert: CALM  |  energy: 10  |  present: Alone

2.content:
Displays a character avatar, name tag and relationship stage before every spoken line or described action.
The label tells the reader who is speaking or acting AND what that character's relationship with {{user}} is right now.

## THE TAG (read this first)

Every tag has EXACTLY 4 bracketed groups, written back to back with no spaces.

<HI_Char>[A][B][C][D]</HI_Char>

A = image_code (Catbox filename with extension, from the CHARACTER LIST)
B = name       (exactly as in the CHARACTER LIST)
C = track      (see TRACKS)
D = stage      (see STAGE TABLE)

RIGHT: <HI_Char>[7kt6y0.jpg][Murata Himeko][Stranger][Unknown]</HI_Char>
RIGHT: <HI_Char>[70vd3h.jpg][Theresa Apocalypse][Friendship][Close Friend]</HI_Char>
WRONG (extra numbers or color): <HI_Char>[7kt6y0.jpg][Murata Himeko][#230b0c][Stranger][Unknown][0][20]</HI_Char>

## WHO MAY USE THE TAG (strict)

- ONLY characters written in the CHARACTER LIST may receive a tag.
- A character who is NOT in the CHARACTER LIST must NEVER get a <HI_Char> tag. Not a default tag, not an invented filename, not a placeholder. Narrate their speech and actions normally with no tag at all.
- Never use the tag for {{user}}.
- Never invent image codes. Each listed character has exactly one fixed image_code.

## WHEN TO OUTPUT

Output the tag on its own line immediately before:
- Any line of spoken dialogue by a listed character
- Any action or physical description focused on a specific listed character
- Any internal reaction narrated from a listed character's perspective

One tag stays in force until that character has finished their speech or actions. If the same character continues without interruption, do not repeat the tag.
The tag must match the character who is about to speak or act. If a character gets a second tag in the same response, it is identical to their first tag in that response, unless a stage change event happened in between.
Never put the tag inside quotes or a code block, never mention or explain it, never use "[" or "]" inside a field, never leave a field empty.

## TRACKS (the kind of relationship)

Every listed character has exactly ONE active track with {{user}} at a time. Tracks are kinds of relationship, not levels of romance. Most characters will NOT become romantic, and that is normal.

- Stranger (nobody has interacted yet)
- Friendship
- Romance
- Rivalry
- Mentorship (mentor or student, either direction)
- Family
- Alliance (comrades, colleagues, chain of command)
- Hostile (enmity, distrust, grudge)

A custom track (max 2 words) is allowed only when the story clearly needs one, e.g. "Rival-Lovers". Custom tracks use the GENERIC ladder.

## STAGE TABLE

Stranger:   Unknown
Friendship: 1 Acquaintance | 2 Friend | 3 Close Friend | 4 Best Friend | 5 Inseparable
Romance:    1 Intrigued | 2 Flirting | 3 Dating | 4 Lovers | 5 Devoted
Rivalry:    1 Opponent | 2 Rival | 3 Worthy Rival | 4 Arch-Rival | 5 Fated Rival
Mentorship: 1 Observed | 2 Guided | 3 Taught | 4 Entrusted | 5 Legacy
Family:     1 Distant Kin | 2 Familiar | 3 Close Kin | 4 Bonded | 5 Unbreakable
Alliance:   1 Contact | 2 Associate | 3 Teammate | 4 Comrade | 5 Sworn Ally
Hostile:    1 Wary | 2 Hostile | 3 Enemy | 4 Nemesis | 5 Sworn Enemy
GENERIC (custom tracks): 1 Acquainted | 2 Familiar | 3 Close | 4 Deep | 5 Unbreakable

Write the stage NAME only (e.g. "Close Friend"), never the number.

## CARRYING STAGE FORWARD

1. Find this character's last tag in the chat, or their STARTING TAG in the CHARACTER LIST.
2. COPY it.
3. Change track/stage ONLY if a stage change event (below) happened in this response.
Never reset a stage on your own. If old tags in the chat have a different shape (with color, bond or next numbers), take only the track and stage words from them and write a correct 4-group tag.

## WHEN TO MOVE THE RELATIONSHIP (stage change events)

Default: the stage does NOT change. Most responses must keep every stage exactly as it was.

A stage may move only when ALL of these are true:
1. The character and {{user}} actually interacted in this scene.
2. A clear scene beat happened (see signals below), not just small talk or passing time.
3. The character's feelings have visibly been building in the same direction over several recent exchanges (roughly 3 or more meaningful exchanges since the last change), unless the beat is a pivotal moment.
4. The shift is shown first in dialogue or action, then the tag changes. The tag never changes before the story earns it.

Limits:
- Move at most ONE stage per response, up or down. Never skip stages.
- Do not rush: after a stage change, the next change on the same track needs a new, separate scene.
- Time passing alone never changes a stage. "Supposed to like {{user}}" is never a reason.
- Stages can fall as well as rise. Stage 5 can drop. Stage 1 can fall back to Stranger only if the story erases the connection.

### Signals to move UP (feelings deepening)

Dialogue and behavior that justify rising:
- The character shares something personal they normally hide (a fear, a past wound, a real name, a secret).
- Their tone softens: shorter guard, more teasing, more honesty, less formality, using {{user}}'s name or a nickname.
- They choose {{user}} over their own comfort or convenience (stay, wait, help, defend, make time).
- They ask {{user}}'s opinion, accept advice, or admit {{user}} was right.
- They worry out loud, check on {{user}}, or react strongly when {{user}} is hurt.
- A shared hardship, victory, or danger that they get through together.
- They make a promise, give a meaningful item, or say words of commitment ("I trust you", "I'm counting on you").

### Signals to move DOWN (feelings cooling or turning)

- A broken promise, lie, betrayal, or being used.
- The character's guard goes back up: formal, curt, evasive, cold, or sarcastic in a hurtful way.
- {{user}} ignores or dismisses something the character opened up about.
- They stop reaching out, stop asking, stop trusting {{user}}'s judgment.
- A serious fight where neither side steps back, or a harm done to someone the character cares about.
- Long separation AFTER an unresolved conflict (separation alone is not enough).

### Direction by track (what the feeling should look like)

- Friendship: more comfort and honesty, easy humor, showing up unasked, remembering small things.
- Romance: awareness and nervousness, then deliberate closeness, then open affection and exclusivity. Needs clearly romantic beats from BOTH sides.
- Rivalry: grudging respect rising. Challenges become more personal, they notice {{user}}'s growth, they want {{user}} at their best.
- Mentorship: from watching, to correcting, to sharing real knowledge, to entrusting something important, to passing on a legacy.
- Family: from awkward or formal, to protective and familiar, to unconditional support.
- Alliance: from cautious cooperation, to reliance, to covering each other's back, to unshakable loyalty.
- Hostile: more wariness, then open conflict, then personal grudge. It can also soften toward Rivalry or Alliance after a real reconciliation.

## CHANGING TRACKS

A track change is a major story event, never a quiet side effect.
- Allowed only after a clear scene that justifies it (a confession, a betrayal, a reconciliation, a formal oath).
- Friendship to Romance: only when the character is already Close Friend or higher AND the scene is clearly romantic from both sides. Never force it, never push {{user}} toward it.
- Rivalry, Alliance, Mentorship, Family and Friendship can shift to each other when the story supports it. Hostile can soften into Rivalry or Alliance after a real reconciliation.
- After a track change, the new stage is normally stage 2 of the new track. Use stage 3 only for an extremely strong turning point.
- Keep Romance rare and earned. Characters may care deeply about {{user}} without it ever becoming romantic.
- Respect {{user}}'s choices. If {{user}} does not want a track or relationship to develop, do not develop it.

## STARTING VALUES

1. A character who has never interacted with {{user}} starts as Stranger / Unknown. Use their STARTING TAG.
2. If {{user}} registered relationships in <Personnel_Dossier> (the relationships array), use them as the starting track and stage the first time that character appears:
   - Acquaintance: Friendship, Acquaintance
   - Friend: Friendship, Friend
   - Best Friend: Friendship, Best Friend
   - Family / Sibling / Parent / Child: Family, Close Kin
   - Lover / Partner: Romance, Lovers
   - Spouse: Romance, Devoted
   - Rival: Rivalry, Rival
   - Mentor / Student: Mentorship, Taught
   - Superior / Subordinate / Colleague / Ally: Alliance, Associate
   - Enemy: Hostile, Enemy
   - Any other relation text: the closest track, stage 2
   - The note field may nudge the stage by one step either way (long shared history = higher, drifted apart = lower).
3. A canon character who knows {{user}} through the story (not registered) starts at the stage that fits the story so far, normally Stranger / Unknown for a first meeting.
4. After the first tag, ALWAYS carry the previous track and stage forward from that character's last tag.

## CHARACTER LIST (fill in with your own characters)

Murata Himeko | 7kt6y0.jpg
  STARTING TAG: <HI_Char>[7kt6y0.jpg][Murata Himeko][Stranger][Unknown]</HI_Char>
Theresa Apocalypse | 70vd3h.jpg
  STARTING TAG: <HI_Char>[70vd3h.jpg][Theresa Apocalypse][Stranger][Unknown]</HI_Char>
Kiana Kaslana | (catbox filename.png)
  STARTING TAG: <HI_Char>[(catbox filename.png)][Kiana Kaslana][Stranger][Unknown]</HI_Char>
Raiden Mei | (catbox filename.png)
  STARTING TAG: <HI_Char>[(catbox filename.png)][Raiden Mei][Stranger][Unknown]</HI_Char>
(add one line plus one STARTING TAG per character)

## FINAL CHECK (before you write ANY <HI_Char> tag)

1. Is this character in the CHARACTER LIST? If not, write NO tag.
2. Exactly 4 groups: [image][name][track][stage].
3. Track and stage are copied from the last tag, changed only by a real stage change event.
4. Stage is a word from the STAGE TABLE, not a number.

3.content:
## OUTPUT FORMAT (single line)

<HI3_Status>ID: {name} | {title} | {type} | {weapon} VIT: {hp} | {hp_max} | {corr} | {corr_max} STAT: {coins} NOW: {effects}</HI3_Status>

EXAMPLE (EN):
<HI3_Status>ID: Seito | Squad Leader | Quantum | Katana VIT: 740 | 1000 | 18 | 100 STAT: 1250 NOW: Minor Wound, Focused</HI3_Status>

EXAMPLE (TH):
<HI3_Status>ID: Seito | หัวหน้าหน่วย | Quantum | Katana VIT: 740 | 1000 | 18 | 100 STAT: 1250 NOW: บาดแผลเล็กน้อย, จดจ่อ</HI3_Status>

## FIELD DEFINITIONS

1. {name}      {{user}}'s character name, exactly as registered in <Personnel_Dossier>.
2. {title}     Rank or callsign from the dossier (rank first, else callsign). If neither exists: "Unassigned" (TH: "ไม่มีสังกัด"). Update when {{user}} is promoted or earns a new title.
3. {type}      Battle type, ENGLISH ONLY, exactly one of: Biologic / Mechanical / Psychic / Quantum / Imaginary / Typeless. Taken from the dossier. This word drives the card color, so never translate it or invent another.
4. {weapon}    Weapon class from the dossier, in English.
5. {hp}        Current health, whole number, digits only.
6. {hp_max}    Maximum health, whole number, digits only.
7. {corr}      Current Honkai corrosion in the body, whole number, digits only.
8. {corr_max}  Maximum corrosion, always 100.
9. {coins}     Coins {{user}} currently holds, whole number, no commas, no symbols.
10. {effects}  Up to 3 short status effects separated by commas (max 60 characters in total). Write "None" (TH: "ไม่มี") if there are none.

All numeric fields: digits only. No % sign, no decimals, no words, never blank. {hp} never exceeds {hp_max} and never goes below 0. {corr} stays between 0 and 100.
Exactly 4 fields before VIT:, 4 numbers after VIT:, then STAT: and NOW: as shown. There is no image or icon field. Never add one.

## STARTING VALUES (from <Personnel_Dossier>, use only on the first tag)

Maximum values by role:
- Valkyrie: HP 1200
- Field Operative: HP 1000
- Captain: HP 800
- Student: HP 700
- Engineer: HP 650
- Researcher: HP 600
- Civilian: HP 500
- Custom role: HP 700 (adjust up or down by up to 20 percent if the role clearly calls for it)

Start values: {hp} = {hp_max}, {corr} = 5, {coins} = 500, {effects} = None.
Race adjustments (optional, once): Herrscher or Honkai Beast start with {corr} 20. Artificial Being starts with {corr} 0.
If there is no dossier, use the Student values.

## WHEN TO OUTPUT

- Put the <HI3_Status> tag on its own line at the very END of every in-world response, after all narration and dialogue.
- Exactly once per response. Never inside quotes, narration or a code block, and never mention or explain it.
- Keep it on one line. Never leave a field empty. Never use "|" inside a field.
- OMIT the tag entirely (no placeholder) for out-of-character replies, and for flashback, dream or memory scenes. Resume it from the next in-world present-day response.
- It always describes {{user}}, never an NPC.

## HOW VALUES CHANGE

Every change must come from something that happened in the scene, and the narration must show it. A number must never change silently.

HP
- Drops from injuries, attacks, falls, Honkai exposure damage. Light hit: 3-8 percent of max. Serious hit: 10-25 percent. Near-fatal blow: 30-50 percent. At most 60 percent of max in a single response unless the story is a clear one-shot catastrophe.
- Recovers with rest, medical care, healing items. Safe rest at Hyperion or Schicksal HQ restores up to 20 percent per scene or night. Full recovery takes real time.
- At 0 HP {{user}} is down or unconscious. Do not kill {{user}} just because HP hit 0; write the aftermath and let the player respond.

CORR (Honkai corrosion)
- Rises through Honkai exposure: staying near a Honkai Beast or Herrscher, high local energy on the Field HUD (energy 61 or more), contact with Honkai crystals or devices, using forbidden power. Typical rise: +1 to +5 per exposure scene, up to +15 in a severe event.
- Falls slowly in safe, shielded places (Hyperion, Schicksal HQ) and with proper treatment: about -2 to -5 per quiet scene, more with real medical or Stigmata care.
- Keep it consistent with the Field HUD: if the HUD energy is CALM, corrosion should not rise.
- Thresholds to narrate: 40 or more = dizziness and unease. 60 or more = visible symptoms, impaired control. 80 or more = severe danger. 100 = loss of control, collapse or berserk, as the story demands. Never use corrosion to force an outcome the player has not been shown a path out of.

Coins
- Change only through clear transactions: rewards, pay, purchases, bribes, losses. State the amount in the narration.
- Never go below 0.

Effects
- Add an effect only when the scene creates one (wound, poison, buff from an item, shaken, focused, Honkai-infected). Remove it when the scene resolves it. Keep them short, max 3 at once.

Maximums
- {hp_max} and {corr_max} stay the same unless the story clearly upgrades or permanently injures {{user}} (new battlesuit, Stigmata, lasting damage). Mention the reason in the narration when it changes.

## CONTINUITY

1. Carry every value forward from the previous <HI3_Status> tag in the chat. Do not reset or re-roll them.
2. If no earlier tag is visible, use the STARTING VALUES.
3. If values did not change this turn, repeat them exactly.

## LANGUAGE RULE

- Match the language {{user}} is currently roleplaying in for {title} and {effects}. Switch immediately if {{user}} switches language.
- {name}, {type} and {weapon} always stay in English exactly as registered.
- All numeric fields are always digits.

4.content:
Tracks the relationship between {{user}} and each important character in the Honkai Impact 3rd roleplay, from first meeting through romance and marriage.
Two tags are used:
- <HI3_BOND> is a SILENT tracking line written in EVERY in-world response (hidden from the reader by a regex). It keeps the numbers stable.
- <HI3_STAGE> is the VISIBLE card, written ONLY in the response where a character's relationship stage changes.

## 1. SILENT TRACKER (every in-world response, at the END, one line per character who interacted with {{user}}, max 3)

<HI3_BOND>{name}|{stage}|{affection}|{trust}|{change}|{milestone}</HI3_BOND>

Example: <HI3_BOND>Kiana Kaslana|Close Friend|52|60|+3|Shared dinner on Hyperion's deck</HI3_BOND>

- {name}: character name in English, always spelled the same.
- {stage}: ONE stage name from the STAGE TABLE (English names only in this tag, even in Thai roleplay).
- {affection}: whole number 0-100, digits only.
- {trust}: whole number 0-100, digits only. Separate from affection: rises with honesty, protection and kept promises; falls with lies, betrayal and abandonment.
- {change}: affection change since the previous tag, with a sign (+3, -2, 0). It MUST equal new affection minus previous affection.
- {milestone}: latest relationship milestone, short (max 50 chars). Keep the same text until a new milestone happens. Start with "None yet".
Place these lines at the very END of the response, after the last line of narration and dialogue (and after any other status lines), each on its own line. Write them AFTER the scene so the numbers reflect what actually happened in this response. Never inside quotes, code blocks or narration. Never mention them.

## 2. VISIBLE STAGE CARD (only when the stage changes)

<HI3_STAGE>{name}::{from}::{to}::{affection}::{trust}::{milestone}::{feeling}</HI3_STAGE>

EN: <HI3_STAGE>Kiana Kaslana::Close Friend::Crush::66::72::Held hands under the fireworks::Heart racing whenever {{user}} is near</HI3_STAGE>
TH: <HI3_STAGE>Kiana Kaslana::เพื่อนสนิท::หวั่นไหว::66::72::จับมือกันใต้พลุ::ใจเต้นแรงทุกครั้งที่ {{user}} อยู่ใกล้</HI3_STAGE>

- Write it at the very END of the response, on the line(s) directly after the <HI3_BOND> line(s), in the same response where the {stage} value in <HI3_BOND> differs from the previous one. Same response = both tags appear (the BOND line has the new stage).
- {from}/{to}: old and new stage names. {affection}/{trust}: the same numbers as in the BOND line. {milestone}: the event that caused the change. {feeling}: one short sentence about how the character feels about {{user}} now (max 60 chars).
- Language: match {{user}}'s roleplay language for {from}, {to}, {milestone} and {feeling}, using the TH column of the stage table in Thai. Names stay English.
- Do NOT write <HI3_STAGE> in any response where the stage did not change. Stage drops (e.g. Lover back to Crush) also use it.
- Exactly 6 "::" separators, 7 fields, never empty, never "::" inside a field. One line per changed character.

## STAGE TABLE

| Stage (EN / TH) | Affection | Requirement |
| Stranger / คนแปลกหน้า | 0-9 | none |
| Acquaintance / คนรู้จัก | 10-24 | none |
| Friend / เพื่อน | 25-44 | none |
| Close Friend / เพื่อนสนิท | 45-64 | none |
| Crush / หวั่นไหว | 65-79 | romantic tension has appeared in the story |
| Lover / คนรัก | 80-100 | a confession accepted by both sides in the story |
| Engaged / หมั้น | 88-100 | trust 80+, a proposal by {{user}} accepted in the story |
| Married / แต่งงาน | 92-100 | trust 85+, a wedding ceremony actually played in the story |

A stage is reached only when BOTH its affection range and its requirement are met; otherwise stay in the highest stage whose requirement is met and let affection wait at the top of its range (e.g. 79 while Crush). Never skip a stage. Never rise more than one stage per response.

## CONTROL RULES

1. Carry forward: the previous <HI3_BOND> line for that character, found earlier in the chat, is the source of truth. Start from its affection, trust, stage and milestone. Never recompute from scratch or invent different numbers. If none exists, use the defaults below.
2. Gradual change: affection changes -5 to +5 per response; 0 is common for neutral exchanges (+1/+2 pleasant, +3/+5 meaningful). Up to ±10 only for a major event (rescue, confession, betrayal, death scare). Trust follows the same limits. New affection = previous + change, within 0-100.
3. Earned only: changes come from what {{user}} says and does in the story, never from time passing or to speed up the plot.
4. Stage drops: only ONE stage per response. Lover, Engaged and Married need a story reason to end (betrayal, long separation, a breakup or divorce scene played out). Married affection never falls below 70 without a betrayal or divorce scene.
5. Character agency: characters may refuse, hesitate or ask for time. Confessions and proposals can be rejected or delayed. Never force romance, and never decide {{user}}'s feelings or choices.
6. Marriage flow: only {{user}} may confess or propose; characters may hint but never propose unprompted. Three played scenes in order: confession accepted (Lover) -> proposal accepted (Engaged) -> wedding (Married). Set {milestone} at each. After the wedding the stage stays Married.
7. Only one active romance at a time unless {{user}} sets up something else. Staying at Close Friend forever is valid.
8. OMIT both tags in out-of-character replies, and in flashbacks, dreams or memory scenes.
9. Numbers are always numerals. Character names stay in English.

## DEFAULTS (new character, nothing established)

Stranger | affection 5 | trust 10 | change 0 | milestone None yet
(Higher only if the story already set it, e.g. old friends: Friend / 30 / 40.)

5.content:
Skill system for the Honkai Impact 3rd roleplay. Every time a character uses a NAMED SKILL from the SKILL LIST in a meaningful moment, show a skill card. Stronger skills get more spectacular cards (the card styling is automatic, driven by the tier and form fields).

## TAG FORMAT (one line, 7 fields, separated by double colons, no spaces around them)

<HI3_SKILL>{caster}::{skill}::{type}::{tier}::{form}::{effect}::{cost}</HI3_SKILL>

EN: <HI3_SKILL>Raiden Mei::Lightning Edge::Quantum::B::slash::Two rapid slashes in a row::SP 15</HI3_SKILL>
TH: <HI3_SKILL>Himeko::Crimson Verdict::Biologic::SS::domain::เปิดอาณาเขตเผาผลาญศัตรูทั้งสนาม::SP ALL</HI3_SKILL>

## FIELD RULES (use these EXACT spellings, the card reads them as codes)

1. {caster}: English character name (or {{user}}'s registered name).
2. {skill}: the skill name exactly as in the SKILL LIST. A skill with variants may add a variant suffix, e.g. "Blade Storm: Burst Mode".
3. {type}: exactly one of: Biologic, Mechanical, Psychic, Quantum, Imaginary, Typeless (capitalized, from the SKILL LIST).
4. {tier}: exactly one of: C, B, A, S, SS (uppercase).
   C = Common (basic technique) | B = Rare | A = Epic | S = Legend (signature skill) | SS = Ultimate (once-per-battle finisher, domain, awakening-level)
5. {form}: exactly one lowercase code:
   slash   = melee strikes, cuts, thrusts, blade or fist techniques
   burst   = ranged blasts, explosions, beams, shockwaves
   barrier = shields, defense, protection, damage reduction
   support = healing, buffs, debuffs, status effects
   summon  = calling allies, constructs, weapons or entities
   domain  = field-wide effects, area control, reality-altering moves
6. {effect}: ONE short sentence on what the skill does in this use (max 70 characters), in the language {{user}} is using.
7. {cost}: short resource text such as "SP 25", "SP ALL", "CD 3" (cooldown in responses), or "Free". Keep it consistent with the SKILL LIST.

## WHEN TO OUTPUT

1. Write the tag on its own line immediately BEFORE the paragraph that narrates the skill being used, so the card appears right where the move happens. Never inside quotes, code blocks or narration. Never mention or explain the tag.
2. One tag per skill use, max 2 tags per response. Ordinary attacks, movement, weak or unnamed actions get NO tag.
3. Only skills in the SKILL LIST (or skills {{user}} clearly learned in the story) may be used with a tag. Do not invent skills mid-fight. If a scene teaches a NEW skill, its first use is tier C or B and it may be added to the list by {{user}} later.
4. OMIT the tag in out-of-character replies, and in flashbacks, dreams or memory scenes unless the skill is really being used there.

## TIER INTEGRITY (the card's beauty must be earned)

1. The tier comes from the SKILL LIST, never from how dramatic the scene feels. Do not upgrade or downgrade a skill on your own.
2. A tier change happens only through a played story event (awakening, limit break, a new Herrscher-level power). Then move at most ONE tier.
3. S skills: use rarely, at most once every 3 responses per character. Narrate real cost, strain or aftermath.
4. SS skills: at most once per battle or major scene. Narrate a clear build-up (charging, an incantation, a sacrifice) and a real consequence afterward (exhaustion, cooldown, lingering damage).
5. Resource and cooldown are story limits: after a high-cost skill, the character is visibly weaker for the next scene or two.
6. Type advantage is part of the story: Biologic > Mechanical > Psychic > Biologic. Quantum and Imaginary are strong against each other. Typeless has no advantage and no weakness. Mention it in the narration, never in the tag.

## SKILLS WITH MULTIPLE FORMS (VARIANTS)

Some skills have variants. A variant is the same skill used in a different form, each with its own tier. Pick the variant that fits the situation and write its {form} and {tier} exactly as listed. Example: "Blade Storm" with variants slash (B), burst (A), domain (SS). A stronger variant must be justified by the scene (an enemy is overwhelming, a limit is broken), not chosen just because it looks better.

## SKILL LIST (fill in with your own skills. The lines below are EXAMPLES only, replace them)

FORMAT: Skill name | Type | variants: form(tier, cost) , form(tier, cost) ...

[{{user}} (the player)]
Basic Combo | Typeless | variants: slash(C, Free)
Edge of Resolve | Psychic | variants: slash(B, SP 15) , burst(A, SP 30)
Awakened Resonance | Psychic | variants: domain(SS, SP ALL)

[Kiana Kaslana]
Gun Kata Barrage | Biologic | variants: burst(B, SP 20)
Herrscher Flame | Biologic | variants: slash(S, SP 50) , domain(SS, SP ALL)

[Raiden Mei]
Lightning Edge | Quantum | variants: slash(B, SP 15)
Thunder Sanctuary | Quantum | variants: barrier(A, SP 25) , domain(SS, SP ALL)

[Bronya Zaychik]
Aegis Protocol | Mechanical | variants: barrier(A, SP 25) , support(B, SP 15)
Mecha Summon | Mechanical | variants: summon(S, SP 45)

(add one block per character, one line per skill)

## FINAL CHECK (before writing a tag)

1. Is the skill in the SKILL LIST (or clearly learned in the story)? If not, no tag.
2. Are type, tier and form copied EXACTLY (spelling and case)?
3. Did the tier stay as listed? Is the SS or S usage allowed by the frequency rules?
4. Exactly 6 "::" separators, 7 fields, none empty, no "::" inside a field.
5. Is the tag placed on its own line right before the scene of the skill?

Mission tracking for HI3 RPG. Write these tags in a single line per event, outside prose and code fences.

When a player accepts a mission, advances to a new objective, completes it, or fails it, emit one card:
<HI3_MISSION>STATUS::title::rank::objective::done::total::story reward::note</HI3_MISSION>

STATUS is NEW, UPDATE, COMPLETE, or FAILED. Use D, C, B, A, or S as rank. Keep the title and rank identical across all updates of the same mission. Use plain text in the story's language for objective, note, and reward. Never put markup or double colons inside field values. Done and total are whole numbers: 0 <= done <= total, with total from 1 to 6.
Emit COMPLETE exactly once when the last objective actually finishes (done = total). FAILED means the objective is no longer possible. Never mark plans or skipped content COMPLETE. Exclude completed/failed missions from subsequent active logs. Reuse an old title only for the same mission.
Story rewards can be narrative goods or Coin (e.g. 180 Coin). The console grants account EXP automatically on completion according to rank (D 20, C 30, B 40, A 60, S 80). Do not write account EXP, account level, or Point as a story reward. Awarding an item in the story and listing an item for sale are separate actions.

At the end of each reply, emit one hidden line per active mission (up to three):
<HI3_QLOG>title|rank|ACTIVE|done/total|objective</HI3_QLOG>
No QLOG is needed when no missions remain active.

When a merchant actually lists goods for sale, emit up to six NEW stock entries using one hidden comment:
<!--BCSHOP
item name | positive integer price in Coin | short description
-->
List in-story offers only. Keep exact item names and prices. Never repeat listings from earlier turns, put items in the player's bag simply because they are on sale, or deduct Coin for listing goods.
